t.6.85.1: As the army was swiftly slaughtered in that great battle, the two sides, striking at one another, became like a lake almost wholly dried up in the fierce heat of summer.
t.6.85.2: At the destruction of his own army and the slaying of Virūpākṣa, Rāvaṇa, lord of the rākṣasas, became twice as enraged.
t.6.85.3: Seeing his army wasted away and being slain by the monkeys, and beholding this reversal of fortune in battle, he was seized with anguish.
t.6.85.4: And he said to Mahodara, the subduer of foes, who stood close by: "At this time, O mighty-armed one, my hope of victory rests in you."
t.6.85.6: Thus addressed, Mahodara said "So be it" to the lord of the rākṣasas, and he entered the enemy army like a moth entering a fire.
t.6.85.5: Slay the enemy host, O hero, and display your valor today. This is the time to repay the master's bread; let the fighting be done well.
t.6.85.7: Then that mighty and splendid one, urged on by his master's command and by his own valor, wrought a slaughter of the monkeys.
t.6.85.8: Seeing the great army of the vānaras shattered in battle, Sugrīva then rushed straight at Mahodara.
t.6.85.9: Seizing a huge and dreadful rock as large as a mountain, the lord of the monkeys, of great energy, hurled it to slay him.
t.6.85.10: Seeing that formidable rock suddenly hurtling toward him, Mahodara, undismayed, then shattered it with his arrows.
t.6.85.11: Cut into a thousand pieces by that rākṣasa with floods of arrows, the rock fell to the ground like a scattered flock of circling vultures.
t.6.85.13: Then he, enraged, saw an iron club lying on the ground. Whirling that blazing club and displaying it to him, he struck his excellent horses swiftly with the tip of the club.
t.6.85.12: Seeing that rock shattered, Sugrīva, overcome with rage, uprooted a sāla tree and hurled it at the rākṣasa at the forefront of the battle; but that hero, conqueror of enemy cities, split it apart with his arrows.
t.6.85.14: Then the heroic rākṣasa Mahodara, enraged, leapt down from that great chariot whose horses had been slain and seized a mace.
t.6.85.15: Those two heroes, holding mace and iron club in their hands, clashed in battle, roaring like two mighty bulls, like two thunderclouds flashing with lightning.
t.6.85.16: The lord of the monkeys struck his mace with an iron club; that club of his, shattered by the mace, fell to the surface of the earth.
t.6.85.17: Then the splendid Sugrīva seized from the surface of the earth a terrible iron club, adorned all over with gold.
t.6.85.19: Then, their weapons shattered, the two closed in on each other with their fists, filled with fiery energy and strength, like two blazing fires.
t.6.85.18: Raising it up, he hurled it, and the other in turn hurled another mace; the two, striking against each other, were shattered and fell to the surface of the earth.
t.6.85.20: Then the two struck each other and roared again and again; and having struck each other with their palms, they fell upon the surface of the earth.
t.6.85.21: Then the two unconquered heroes swiftly leapt up and struck each other, and with their arms they hurled one another about.
t.6.85.22: Then the rākṣasa Mahodara, of tremendous speed, seized a sword that lay close at hand, together with a shield.
t.6.85.23: In the same way Sugrīva, the foremost of monkeys and exceedingly swift, seized the great sword that had fallen together with its shield.
t.6.85.25: And the two of them swiftly circled each other in a rightward sweep, both enraged at one another, both wholly bent upon victory.
t.6.85.24: Those two, their limbs seized by fury, rushed at each other roaring, swords raised, exultant in battle, both masters of weapons in combat.
t.6.85.26: But that heroic Mahodara, of great speed, boastful of his prowess and evil-minded, brought that sword crashing down upon the great shield.
t.6.85.27: As the rākṣasa was pulling out his sword where it had stuck fast, the elephant among monkeys struck off with his own sword his head, helmet and all, adorned with earrings.
t.6.85.28: Seeing him fallen on the surface of the earth with his head cut off, that army of the lord of the rākṣasas did not stand its ground there.
t.6.85.29: Having slain him, the delighted monkey roared together with the vānaras; Daśagrīva was filled with rage, while Rāghava shone with joy.
